mobilier.short: Priced from a sketch: fabrics, finishes, lead times.
mobilier.panel: Customers do not think in production terms. The agent asks in the order you would ask yourself — space, material, deadline — and hands sales a request that is ready to price.

dialog.text: What are the dimensions of the wall you are furnishing?
3.2 metres, with a window in the middle.
Fabric or leather? I can show you the price difference on the same configuration.

constructii.name: Renovation and interior design
constructii.short: Quoted by area: stages, crews, schedules.
constructii.panel: A quote starts from the area and from the state the space is in right now. The agent finds out both before a site visit takes up your day.

dialog.text: What is the area, and what state is the space in now?
68 m², a new flat, bare shell.
Full renovation or finishes only? The quote differs by a factor of two.

imobiliare.name: Developers and estate agencies
imobiliare.short: Requirements, budget, a viewing in the calendar.
imobiliare.panel: Budget and timing are settled in the first two questions. The agent asks them, and the estate agent gets a qualified lead with a viewing already proposed.

dialog.text: What budget do you have in mind, and by when?
Up to €90,000, by spring.
I have three options within budget. Does Saturday morning suit you for a viewing?

auto.name: Car dealerships
auto.panel: Configuration, financing and the test drive are three conversations usually held separately. The agent keeps all three inside one.

dialog.text: What do you drive now, and what is missing?
An estate, but I need more space.
Two configurations fit. Shall we book a test drive on Saturday?

energie.name: Solar and HVAC
energie.panel: The payback calculation depends on consumption and on the roof. The agent collects both and sends the quote with the payback period already worked out.

dialog.text: How much do you pay for electricity each month?
Around 2,400 lei.
What kind of roof do you have? The number of panels depends on it.

clinici.name: Dental and aesthetic medicine
clinici.panel: Questions about pain, price and recovery time are hard to ask a person and easy to ask an agent. The patient reaches reception already decided.

dialog.text: What is bothering you, and for how long?
I need an implant, but I am afraid of the pain.
I will explain exactly how it goes and what it costs. Do you prefer mornings?

hero.title: AI agents for businesses where the price is calculated
hero.lead: Rent the agent you need — configured for your niche and your brand, on a monthly subscription. No implementation project, no technical team.

problem.title: The quote is being worked out. Meanwhile the customer is asking somewhere else.

afterHours.title: The question arrives after hours
afterHours.text: Most enquiries land in the evening and at weekends. The answer goes out the next morning — by which time the person has written to three other firms and is comparing.

everyRequestDiffers.title: Every enquiry is different
everyRequestDiffers.text: Dimensions, materials, lead times, budget. Until you have all of them there is nothing to price — and each round of clarification costs another day.

sameAnswers.title: Your salesperson repeats the same ten answers
sameAnswers.text: Their time goes into questions whose answer never changes, instead of the quotes that actually close.

agents.title: Six agents. Rent only the ones you need.
agents.lead: Each agent is a separate product, configured for your niche and your brand. Start with one, add another once the first has shown its result.

custom.title: Need something else?
custom.text: Tell us what the agent should do in your business and we will tell you whether it can be done.

industries.title: Configured for your niche
industries.lead: Not "for any business": different questions, different materials, a different route to the price. Pick your industry and see what the conversation looks like.
industries.otherText: We work in niches that are not on this list too. If the price has to be calculated, the script can be configured.

onboarding.title: From the first conversation to an agent on your site
onboarding.lead: This is not an implementation project. You need no developer, no IT department and no new website — the agent sits on top of what you already have.

talk.title: The conversation
talk.text: What you sell, how the price is worked out at your company, and what people ask you most often. Nothing to prepare in advance.

materials.title: The materials
materials.text: Website, product sheets, price list, terms. In whatever form they exist — Excel, PDF, Word, photos. Putting them in order is our job.
materials.time: As long as an email takes

config.title: The configuration
config.text: The script for your niche, your pricing rules, your brand on the quote. You see the agent before your customers do and correct anything that does not sound like you.

embed.title: One line of code
embed.text: A script on your site. The widget runs isolated from the page styles, so it breaks nothing you already have. If there is nobody to do it, we do it.

onboarding.total: Usually under two hours of your time in total. The rest is on us — including the unpleasant part, where the price list has to be read line by line.

talk.a: What you sell and what a typical order looks like
talk.b: How the price is worked out at your company
talk.c: What people ask you most often

embed.label: The script on your site
embed.note: One line, at the end of the page. The widget runs isolated from the site styles.

pricing.title: Three packages, fixed contents
pricing.lead: You pay monthly for the agents that run. Separately, once at the start, you pay for the setup: reading your materials and turning your price list into the rules the agent prices by.

portal.title: One place where you see everything the agent did
portal.lead: The agent works on your site. What comes out of that work — requests, quotes, numbers — waits for you in the portal, not scattered across an inbox.
portal.panelText: Every client has their own portal with their own data. You do not ask us for a report and wait until we send it — you log in and look. Included in every package, from Start upwards.

capabilities.leads: Leads — every request, with everything the customer said
capabilities.offers: Quotes — every PDF issued, with its number and date
capabilities.stats: Statistics — where people stop and what they ask
capabilities.agents: Agents — switch on, switch off, correct the answers

portal.cta: See the portal in a demo

faq.title: What people ask before they start
faq.lead: If your question is not here,

timeline.q: How long until the agent is on my site?
timeline.a: From your side — one conversation and the materials you already have. The timeline depends on the shape your price list is in: a spreadsheet is one thing, a scanned catalogue is another. We give you a concrete date after the first conversation, not before.

setup.q: What is the setup fee, and why is it paid separately?
setup.a: It is the work at the start, done once: we read your materials line by line, turn your price list into the rules the agent prices by, write the script for your niche and check it all together with you before launch. The monthly subscription covers the agent running, not that work. The amount depends on the package and is written under the price.

unknown.q: What does the agent do when it does not know the answer?
unknown.a: It does not invent one. It answers from your materials, and when the answer is not there it says it will check and captures the request, with everything discussed up to that point. Your salesperson gets the conversation, not an "interested lead".

data.q: Where does my customers' data go?
data.a: It stays yours and is isolated from every other client on the platform — not by a promise, but by the way the database is built. One account cannot reach another account's data.

site.q: Do I have to change my website?
site.a: No. One script is added, and that is all. The widget runs isolated from the page styles, so it cannot break what you have — not the fonts, not the layout. If there is nobody to add it, we do it.

language.q: What language does the agent speak?
language.a: Whichever one it is written to, among those configured for you. Romanian, Russian and English are the ones we work with most often. How many are active depends on the package: Start includes one, Growth two, and Platform is agreed individually. We match the tone to how you speak to your customers, not to a manual.

priceChange.q: What happens when I change my prices?
priceChange.a: You send us the new list. The agent prices by rules rather than by figures written by hand into answers, so a price change does not require reconfiguring from scratch.

cancel.a: Yes, it is monthly. What happens to your data and to quotes already issued after you stop is written in the contract, and you read it before signing, not after.

reviews.q: Why are there no reviews or client logos on this site?
reviews.a: Because we do not have enough of them yet to mean anything. The platform is being run in on a real client in made-to-order furniture, whom we do not name until they agree. We would rather show no logos than logos that do not tell the truth.

finalCta.title: See the agent on your own products, not on a generic demo
finalCta.lead: In the demo we take a few products from your catalogue and show you exactly what the agent would answer a real customer.
finalCta.note: No hour-long presentation. Thirty minutes and the agent on screen.

portal.text: Every conversation, with its full context. Nothing stays only in the chat window.

chatbot.conversationNote: An example for made-to-order furniture. The prices in the answer come from the client's list, not from us.

dialog.text: Hello. How much would a kitchen along a 3.2 metre wall cost?
That depends first of all on the fronts and the worktop. Do you have a preference — painted MDF, veneer or foil?
Painted MDF. And a stone worktop.
For 3.2 m with painted MDF and a quartz worktop, the range in our list is 38,000 – 46,000 lei, depending on the hardware and the appliances.
And how long does it take?
Production takes around 30 working days from the moment the design is confirmed. If you leave me an email I will send the exact quote today — do you have a photo or a drawing of the space?

chatbot.faqTitle: What people ask about the chatbot

faq.q: How long until it is on my site?
faq.a: From your side — one conversation and the materials you already have. The timeline depends on the shape your price list is in: a spreadsheet is one thing, a scanned catalogue is another. We give you a concrete date after the first conversation.

faq.q: What if it answers something wrong?
faq.a: You see every conversation in the portal. When something sounds wrong, the source it answered from gets corrected — and the correction takes effect immediately, not in the next release. Mistakes in the first week are normal, which is exactly why you read the conversations.

faq.q: Can it take orders and payments?
faq.a: It can collect the complete request and hand it to your salesperson. Order confirmation and payment stay with you — we do not want an agent taking money on your behalf.

faq.q: What happens to my customers' data?
faq.a: It stays yours and is isolated from every other client on the platform — not by a promise, but by the way the database is built.

faq.q: Does it work on a phone?
faq.a: Yes, and it is designed for the small screen first: that is where most questions come from. The window does not cover the page and closes with one gesture.

chatbot.closingTitle: See the chatbot answering about your own products
chatbot.closingLead: In the demo we take a few products from your catalogue and show you exactly what it would answer a real customer.

configurator.metaTitle: AI request configurator — a specification ready to price
configurator.metaDescription: An AI agent that asks the questions the price depends on and hands your sales team a structured specification: dimensions, materials, installation, deadline. Included in the Growth package.
configurator.title: A configurator that collects the specification, not just the contact details
configurator.lead: It asks, one at a time, the questions the price depends on: dimensions, materials, installation, deadline. Your salesperson gets a filled-in sheet and goes straight to pricing, without three days of messages back and forth.

spec.title: Request specification
spec.pending: Distance from the panel board to the roof
spec.footer: 6 of 7 points, filled in from the customer's answers
spec.note: This is the sheet your salesperson will receive. The example is a solar installation — the questions and fields are written for your own niche.

questions.title: It asks in the order that matters
questions.text: No twenty-field form thrown at the visitor. The next question depends on the last answer, the way a salesperson who knows what comes next would ask.

spec.title: It hands over a sheet, not a conversation
spec.text: Your salesperson gets filled-in fields: type, dimensions, material, installation, deadline. No three screens of messages to read before knowing what the person wants.

gaps.title: It says what is missing
gaps.text: What could not be established stays flagged, not guessed. You see what is still to be asked straight away, not halfway through the calculation.

rules.title: It follows your rules
rules.text: Which combinations exist, what cannot be done at all, what needs measuring on site. The rules are yours, not the agent's assumptions.

handoff.title: It arrives where you already work
handoff.text: By email, in the portal, or straight into your CRM as a filled-in record. Your salesperson has no new program to learn.

portal.title: Everything stays in the portal
portal.text: Every sheet, with its date and everything the customer answered. Nothing lives only in one person's inbox.

configurator.sourcesTitle: What the sheet is built from — and what the agent does not do

sourcesYes.title: It collects from
items: Your list of options: materials, dimensions, finishes, installation variants.
Your compatibility rules: what goes with what, and what cannot be done at all.
The questions your salespeople ask today, written down once and asked every time.
What requires measuring or a site visit, so that nothing impossible gets promised.

sourcesNo.title: It never
items: It does not give a final price. It collects the data the price is calculated from; the calculation stays with you.
It does not invent an option that is not on your list.
It does not fill in fields the customer has not confirmed — it leaves them flagged.
It does not send the quote in the salesperson's place, and does not promise a deadline on production's behalf.

configurator.platformsTitle: It starts wherever the request comes in
configurator.platformsLead: The same sheet, wherever the conversation began. The result arrives the same way: filled in, in the portal and by email.
platforms: A link sent to the customer
Filled in by the salesperson, in the portal
configurator.faqTitle: What people ask about the configurator

faq.q: How is it different from an ordinary form?
faq.a: A form asks every question at once, and the same ones for everybody. The configurator asks the next question based on the last answer: if the person said installation is not needed, it does not go on to ask about floors and lifts. The fields stay the same, the road to them is shorter — which is why people reach the end.

faq.q: Does it give the customer a price?
faq.a: No. It collects the data the price depends on and hands the sheet to your salesperson. You do the pricing, with the margin and the exceptions you never write down anywhere. If you want an indicative price said in the conversation itself, that is the chatbot's job, from your own price list.

faq.q: What happens when the customer does not know the answer?
faq.a: It moves on and flags the point. The sheet arrives saying "to clarify: ceiling height", not with an invented value. An empty field you can see is cheaper than a full field that is wrong.

faq.q: Who writes the questions?
faq.a: We do, during setup, from the way you already work: what your salespeople ask, in what order, which combinations are impossible. They are changed from the portal, without asking us.

faq.q: When will it be ready?
faq.a: We do not give a date we cannot keep. It is included in the Growth package: connect it now and the configurator switches on in your account at launch, at the price you joined at.

configurator.closingTitle: See what sheet it would collect from your own requests
configurator.closingLead: At the demo we take one product from your catalogue, write the questions for it, and show you the sheet your salesperson would receive.

crm-assistant.metaTitle: CRM assistant — records filled from the correspondence
crm-assistant.metaDescription: An AI agent that reads the correspondence with your customer and fills in the CRM record: stage, budget, deadline, who decides, the next task. Included in the Growth package.
crm-assistant.title: CRM records filled from the correspondence, not from the salesperson's memory
crm-assistant.lead: It reads the conversation with the customer and puts what changed into the record: the stage, the budget, the deadline, who else decides. Your salesperson confirms rather than types.

record.title: Customer record
record.source: Updated from the email received at 14:02
record.task: Follow up Friday, after their budget meeting
record.note: This is how the record looks after one incoming email. The fields and stages are the ones in your own CRM, not ones we invented.

read.title: It reads the correspondence, not just the forms
read.text: Email, the chat on your site, the messages. That is where the data lives that never reaches a field, because nobody has time to move it by hand.

spec.title: It fills the record, field by field
spec.text: Budget, deadline, the product discussed, the person who decides. The fields are your CRM's; we do not invent extra ones just to have something to fill in.

stage.title: It moves the deal to the stage it is actually at
stage.text: Once the customer has asked for a quote, the deal no longer sits at "new contact". The stage changes from what happened, not from what somebody remembered on Friday evening.

task.title: It sets the next task
task.text: "Follow up Friday, after their budget meeting" — with a date, on the person who owns the customer. Without a task, the follow-up depends on memory.

gaps.title: It does not overwrite what a person wrote
gaps.text: When what the customer says contradicts what is already in the record, the agent flags the difference and leaves the decision to the salesperson.

handoff.title: It stays inside your CRM
handoff.text: We do not move you onto another system and we do not sell you a CRM. The agent writes where you already work.

crm-assistant.sourcesTitle: What it fills the record from — and what it does not do

sourcesYes.title: It fills from
items: The correspondence with the customer: email, the chat on your site, the messages from the channels you connect.
The conversation the chatbot held, if it is already working on your site.
The structure of your own record: the same fields, the same stages, the same names.
The rules for when a new stage begins — written by you, once.

sourcesNo.title: It never
items: It does not delete or overwrite what a person wrote. The difference is flagged; the salesperson decides.
It does not connect to employees' personal mailboxes, and what does not concern the customer in the record does not reach the record.
It does not decide in the salesperson's place: it does not change prices, promise deadlines or close deals.
It does not replace your CRM. It writes into yours; if you do not have one, the records live in the portal.

crm-assistant.platformsTitle: It writes where you keep your customers
crm-assistant.platformsLead: If your system has an API or can receive data through a webhook, the agent writes into it. At the first conversation you tell us what you use and we check before promising.
platforms: The portal, if you have no CRM yet
crm-assistant.faqTitle: What people ask about the CRM assistant

faq.q: Which CRM does it work with?
faq.a: The one that has an API or can receive data through a webhook — which covers most systems in use today. We do not print a list of names to look bigger: you tell us what you use and we check before promising. If you have no CRM, the records live in the portal and export when you move to one.

faq.q: Does the agent see all the company's correspondence?
faq.a: No. It receives only the channels you give it: the sales address, the chat on your site, the messages from connected channels. An employee's personal mailbox is not connected, and what does not concern the customer in the record does not reach the record.

faq.q: What happens if it gets a field wrong?
faq.a: You correct it in the record, like any field. The correction stays in the history: you can see what the agent wrote and what the person changed. If one kind of mistake repeats, we change the rule — not the records, one by one.

faq.q: Do salespeople have to work differently?
faq.a: No. They write to customers exactly as they do now. The difference is that the record is filled in when they open it rather than empty — and that the next task exists without anyone writing it on paper.

faq.q: When will it be ready?
faq.a: We do not give a date we cannot keep. It is included in the Growth package: connect it now and the CRM assistant switches on in your account at launch, at the price you joined at.

crm-assistant.closingTitle: See what it would fill in from your own correspondence
crm-assistant.closingLead: At the demo we take a few real customer conversations — anonymised, if you prefer — and show you what would have reached the record without anyone typing.

follow-up.metaTitle: Follow-up agent — automatic returns to leads that went quiet
follow-up.metaDescription: An AI agent that comes back to customers who never replied: on a schedule you set, about what was actually discussed, on their own channel. It stops the moment they answer. Included in the Growth package.
follow-up.title: It comes back to the customers who went quiet — and stops when they answer
follow-up.lead: Most quotes are not lost on price. They are lost in the silence afterwards. The agent comes back on a schedule you set, writes about what was actually discussed, and stops the moment the person replies.

plan.title: Follow-up plan

steps.text: "Did the quote arrive? If anything in it is unclear, tell me and we'll sort it out."
"The price in the quote holds until the 30th. Shall I hold you a production slot?"

plan.stop: The customer replied on day seven. The remaining follow-ups are cancelled.
plan.note: This is how one lead's plan looks. The number of follow-ups, the intervals and the reasons to stop are the ones you set.

stop.title: It stops when the person answers
stop.text: It does not run the sequence to the end out of inertia. One reply and the rest is cancelled, including what was scheduled a fortnight out.

task.title: It returns on a schedule, not when you happen to remember
task.text: Day two, day six, day twelve — as you decide. It does not depend on who is on holiday or how full the day was.

sources.title: It writes about what was discussed
sources.text: It refers to the product asked about, the price in the quote, the deadline talked through. Not a "still interested?" sent to everybody.

read.title: On the channel the customer came in on
read.text: If they wrote in the chat, they hear back in the chat. If they left an email, they get an email. We do not move them to wherever suits us.

rules.title: You set the limits
rules.text: How many follow-ups, at what intervals, on which days and at what hours, when it stops for good. What you have not allowed does not happen.

portal.title: Every follow-up stays in the portal
portal.text: You can see what was sent, when, and what came of it. Including the leads the agent stopped writing to, and why.

follow-up.sourcesTitle: What it writes the follow-ups from — and what it does not do

sourcesYes.title: It writes from
items: The conversation held with the customer: what they asked for, what was discussed, where it stopped.
The quote that was sent: the items, the price, how long it holds.
The schedule and limits you wrote: how many follow-ups, at what intervals, on which days.
The reasons to stop that you set: they replied, they bought, they asked not to be contacted.

sourcesNo.title: It never
items: It does not write indefinitely. The number of follow-ups is the one you set, and after it the agent stops.
It does not write to people who asked not to be contacted. Not in any scenario and not in any campaign.
It does not invent discounts or extend deadlines to get an answer out of somebody.
It does not write to bought lists or to contacts who never spoke to you.

follow-up.platformsTitle: It comes back where the customer spoke
follow-up.platformsLead: The customer picks the channel, not us. Which ones get connected for you is decided at the first conversation, once we see where your requests actually arrive.
platforms: A task for the salesperson, if you would rather a person called

faq.q: Does it not turn into spam?
faq.a: That depends on the limits, and you set the limits: how many follow-ups, at what intervals, on which days and at what hours. The agent stops at the first reply and never writes to people who asked not to be contacted. One follow-up about a real conversation, to a person who asked you first, is not spam. Three messages a week to a bought list is — and that we do not do.

faq.q: Who writes the follow-up texts?
faq.a: We do, during setup, in the way you speak to your customers, and you see them before the first one goes out. They are changed from the portal, without asking us.

faq.q: What happens if the customer replies angrily?
faq.a: It stops, as it does on any reply, and the conversation reaches the salesperson with everything that was sent before it. The agent does not argue on your behalf.

faq.q: Can I stop the follow-ups for one particular customer?
faq.a: Yes, from the portal, at any time. There is also a stop across the whole base, if you want to suspend follow-ups for a period — over the holidays, during stocktaking, when production is full.

faq.q: When will it be ready?
faq.a: We do not give a date we cannot keep. It is included in the Growth package: connect it now and the follow-up agent switches on in your account at launch, at the price you joined at.

follow-up.closingTitle: See how many of your quotes went quiet
follow-up.closingLead: At the demo we look at the quotes you sent over the last few months and show you what the agent would have written, when — and at which point it would have stopped.

order-status.metaTitle: Order status for customers — automatic updates at each stage
order-status.metaDescription: An AI agent that tells your customer at every stage of the order and gives them a page showing where it stands. It announces delays too, in time. Included in the Growth package.
order-status.title: Your customer finds out where the order is without phoning
order-status.lead: At every stage you mark, a short message goes out with a link to the order page. Delays are announced the same way, and whatever you marked as internal stays internal.

order.title: Order

order.next: When the order goes into finishing

stage.title: It tells them at every stage

task.title: It also says when the date moves

handoff.title: When the customer asks, a person answers

rules.title: What is communicated, and what stays internal

order-status.sourcesTitle: How it knows where the order is — and what it does not do

sourcesYes.title: It finds out from
items: The stages you mark: gone into production, in finishing, ready to ship.
The system you keep orders in, if it has an API or can send data out.
The spreadsheet the records live in, if that is where they live — marked in one place only.
The date in the order and any changes to it, the moment you record them.

sourcesNo.title: It never
items: It does not guess where the order is. If a stage was not marked, the agent says nothing — it does not invent a move that did not happen.
It does not promise a date you did not give. The date communicated is the one in your order.
It does not send the customer what you marked as internal: costs, suppliers, the real reasons behind a delay.
It does not answer questions about the order in your place. It hands them to the person who owns it.

order-status.platformsTitle: It reaches the customer where they read
order-status.platformsLead: A short message and a link to the order page. The page opens with no account and no password: one order, one link, nothing for the customer to install.
order-status.faqTitle: What people ask about order status

faq.q: How does the agent know where the order is?
faq.a: From what you mark. If you keep orders in a system with an API, it reads them from there; if you keep them in a spreadsheet, they are marked there; if you keep them nowhere, they are marked in the portal, from a single screen. What was not marked is not communicated — the agent has no way of knowing on its own what is happening on the shop floor.

faq.q: What happens when an order runs late?
faq.a: The delay is announced, if that is what you chose. You either write the reason or you do not: the customer learns that the date moved and what the new one is, not why it moved. What is internal stays internal.

faq.q: Can the customer reply to the message?
faq.a: Yes, and the reply reaches the person who owns the order, with the full context. An automatic message you cannot reply to is worse than no message at all.

faq.q: Does the workshop have to learn a new program?
faq.a: No. Marking a stage is one tap, from a phone or from the portal. If you already have a system where stages are marked, nothing changes in the way you work.

faq.q: When will it be ready?
faq.a: We do not give a date we cannot keep. It is included in the Growth package: connect it now and the order status agent switches on in your account at launch, at the price you joined at.

order-status.closingTitle: See what your order looks like to your customer
order-status.closingLead: At the demo we take the real stages from your process and show you what messages the customer would get and what they would see on the order page.

content-engine.sourcesTitle: What it writes from — and what it does not do

sourcesYes.title: It writes from
items: Photos and clips of your own jobs, taken the way you already take them: on a phone, on site, at the installation.
The project's own data: materials, dimensions, lead time, the town the job was done in.
The way you already talk about your work — from the texts, quotes and posts you have.
What worked and what did not: old posts that got a response stay as examples, and so do the ones that got none.

sourcesNo.title: It does not
items: It does not invent jobs. No photo and no project means no post — it will not generate an interior that is not yours.
It does not publish on its own. Every text and every frame goes through your approval, and nothing reaches an account you have not given it access to.
It does not write prices, discounts or lead times you never gave. A number that appears in a post becomes a promise.
It does not hold the conversation in comments and messages for you. Questions about price go to a person — or to the chat agent, if you have one.

content-engine.platformsLead: Text and frame are prepared separately for each platform. Publishing happens on the accounts you give us access to; where you give none, you get the material ready to post yourself.
platforms: Ready-made material, if you publish yourself

faq.q: Who decides what gets published?
faq.a: You do. The agent prepares the drafts, but between the text and the publishing there is a press of your button. Automatic publishing can be switched on for a certain kind of post, if at some point you want that — but it is not how you start and not what we recommend.

faq.q: Where does it get the photos?
faq.a: From you. An installation photographed on a phone is enough; no photo shoot is needed. What you do not give it does not appear: the agent does not search the internet for images and does not generate interiors that are not yours.

faq.q: Won't it show that the texts were written by a machine?
faq.a: It shows when a text is written out of nothing. Here it starts from a real job, with its material, its dimensions and its lead time, and the way of writing is taken from what you have already written. And you read it before it goes out anyway.

faq.q: How many posts come out per month?
faq.a: It depends on how many jobs you do and how many of them you manage to photograph. We do not sell a number: a hundred posts from a single project would be a hundred variants of the same thing. We set the rhythm together, on the calendar.

faq.q: When will it be ready?
faq.a: We do not give a date we cannot keep. It is included in the Growth package: if you connect it now, the content engine switches on for your account at launch, at the price you connected at.

questions.q: "How much does a three-metre kitchen cost?"
questions.a: The question with no short answer — and the one you get before anything else. The agent asks what it needs in order to give a range, instead of answering "it depends".
With a photo from Instagram, no name and no code. The agent knows your fabric catalogue and says whether it exists and which price group it falls into.
Lead time depends on the workshop load and on materials. The agent answers with the lead time you set, not one it made up.
Before a survey you need rough dimensions and a budget. The agent collects them, so the trip is not wasted.

mobilier.faqTitle: What workshops ask before they start

faq.q: My prices are not fixed, they are worked out every time. How can the agent answer?
faq.a: That is exactly why it starts with questions. The agent does not hold a list of final prices, but the rules you price by: price per linear metre, coefficient per fabric group, additions for hardware. A range comes out of those, and the exact quote stays with you.

faq.q: My fabric catalogue is a PDF from the supplier. Is that enough?
faq.a: Yes. PDF, Excel, photos of the samples — we take them in whatever form they are in. Putting them in order is our part of the work, and that is what the initial setup pays for.

faq.q: What if the customer asks for a discount?
faq.a: The agent does not give discounts. It says the question is for a salesperson and flags the request — so you know the person asked about price before you call.

faq.q: We also work from designers' drawings. Does the agent get confused?
faq.a: Not if you tell it from the start that there are two flows. A customer who arrives with a drawing gets different questions from one who arrives with an idea — that is settled during configuration.

faq.q: What counts as a conversation?
faq.a: One dialogue with a visitor, however many messages it contains. If the person comes back a few days later and writes again, that is a new conversation. Your own test messages are not counted.

faq.q: What does the setup fee cover?
faq.a: The conversation, reading your materials line by line, turning your price list into the rules the agent prices by, the script for your niche, your brand on the quote, and checking it together with you before launch. It is paid once, at the start.

faq.q: Can I change package?
faq.a: Yes, in both directions, from the start of the following month. Moving up, you pay the difference in setup if the new package takes more work.

faq.q: What happens if I exceed the conversation limit?
faq.a: The agent does not stop and customers are not left without an answer. The excess is covered by an additional conversation pack, and if it repeats month after month we suggest moving to the next package — it usually works out cheaper.

faq.q: Is there a minimum contract term?
faq.a: No. The subscription is monthly and can be stopped from the following month. What happens to your data and to quotes already issued after you stop is written in the contract, and you read it before signing.

agentsHub.pathLead: The order is not ours, it is the customer's: they ask, they decide, they go quiet, they buy, they wait. The last agent closes the circle and brings the next person to the first question.

order-status.without: The customer calls to ask where the order is. Three times. And still does not know.

privacyPage.metaDescription: What data the form on this site collects, why, who else sees it and how long we keep it. One technical cookie. No analytics, no pixels, no selling of data.
privacyPage.title: Privacy policy
privacyPage.lead: Written for what this site actually does, not copied from somewhere. If you find something in it that does not match what you see, write to us — the mistake is ours.

sections.title: Who is responsible for the data
sections.intro: Data sent through this site is received by the controller below. Requests about your rights go to the same place.

sections.title: What data we receive
sections.intro: The site has a single form. From it we receive only what you write:
list: Your name — so we know how to address you.
Your email or phone — so we can answer.
Your company's website, if you fill it in. It is optional.
Your message, if you write one. It is optional.
sections.outro: In addition, like any site, the server logs requests: IP address, time, the page requested and the browser type. These logs are technical and are not linked to the form.

sections.title: Why we receive it
sections.intro: We use the form data to answer you and to prepare the demo or the quote you asked for — that is, for the steps before a possible contract, at your own request. Server logs exist so the site can run and be defended against abuse; the basis is our legitimate interest in keeping a service working.
sections.outro: We do not use it for anything else. If you write to us about furniture, we will not write to you a month later about something unrelated.

sections.title: Who else sees it
sections.intro: Besides us, the data passes through two services, each with a strict role:
list: Vercel — hosts the site. Requests to pages go through it, and it keeps the technical logs.
Resend — delivers the email with your request to us. The contents of the form pass through this service on the way to our mailbox.
sections.outro: We give it to nobody else. We do not sell it, trade it, or send it to advertising networks.

sections.title: Where it goes and how long we keep it
sections.intro: A form submission is not saved into a database: it leaves by email and stays in our correspondence. A database for a single form would mean backups, migrations and personal data somebody has to answer for — with no gain for you.
sections.outro: We keep the correspondence for as long as the discussion is live and for twelve months after the last message, so we can pick the conversation back up if you return. After that we delete it. Technical logs are kept by the hosting provider, for a short period, under its own rules.

sections.title: Cookies
sections.intro: The site sets a single cookie, called NEXT_LOCALE. It remembers which language you are reading in, so the next page does not send you to the wrong version. It identifies nobody and tracks nothing.
list: We have no analytics: no Google Analytics, nothing of that kind.
We have no advertising pixels and no social buttons that load somebody else's code.
Fonts are served from our own domain, not from a third-party CDN — your browser asks nothing of another server.
sections.outro: That is why the site does not greet you with a consent banner: there is nothing to consent to.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.intro: Over the data we hold about you, you have the right:
list: To find out what data we hold and to receive a copy.
To ask us to correct what is wrong.
To ask us to delete it.
To ask us to restrict its use, or to object to use based on our legitimate interest.
To receive the data in a format that can be moved elsewhere.
sections.outro: Write to the address above and we will answer within a month at the latest. If the answer does not satisfy you, you have the right to complain to the data protection supervisory authority of the country you live in.

sections.title: What we do not do
list: We do not sell or rent the data to anyone.
We do not build profiles and do not make automated decisions about you.
We do not add you to any mailing list because you filled in the form.
We do not track which pages you read before writing.

sections.title: Your own customers' data
sections.intro: This policy is about the site. If you become a client and an agent ends up processing your customers' data, that is governed separately, by contract and by a data processing agreement, in which you are the controller and we are the processor.
sections.outro: Each client's data stays isolated: we do not mix it between accounts and we do not train anything on it for other clients.

sections.title: Changes
sections.intro: If we change how we work with data, we change this text too, and the date at the top is updated. If the change is significant, we say so visibly rather than quietly replacing a paragraph.

termsPage.metaDescription: What this site is, what the displayed prices mean, what «coming soon» means and what we do not promise. Written short, without paragraphs that say nothing.
termsPage.title: Terms and conditions
termsPage.lead: The site is a presentation, not a shop: nothing is bought from it and no account is created. The text below says what it does mean, then.

sections.title: What the site is
sections.intro: A presentation of AI agents rented on a monthly subscription. It has no cart, no online payment and no user accounts. The only possible action is the form through which you write to us.
sections.outro: Sending the form does not conclude any contract and does not oblige us to accept the work, just as it obliges you to nothing.

sections.title: The prices shown
sections.intro: The prices on the pricing page are the monthly subscription and the one-off setup fee for the standard packages. They are informational: they do not constitute a binding offer in the legal sense, and the contract is concluded separately, in writing.
list: For the Platform package the price is set individually, because the work is different every time.
Prices may change for the future. A client already connected does not have the price changed for the package they hold, under the terms of their contract.
VAT treatment and the invoicing currency are stated in the contract and on the invoice.

sections.title: Agents marked «coming soon»

It does not mean a particular date: we do not promise deadlines we cannot keep. If an agent does not appear within a reasonable time, you have the right to leave the package under the terms of your contract.

sections.title: The images on the pages
sections.intro: The screens drawn on the pages — the widget conversation, the request sheet, the customer record, the follow-up plan, the order status, the content drafts — are illustrations we built, not captures from a running product. The data in them is invented as an example.
sections.outro: They contain no real customers, real orders or anyone's real prices. We display no client logos, testimonials or performance figures that we cannot prove.

sections.title: The site's content
sections.intro: The texts, structure, code, illustrations and visual identity are ours. You may read them and share links, but you may not copy the content in order to publish it as your own.
sections.outro: The names of other companies or platforms, where they appear, belong to their owners and are used only to say where content goes or where data comes from.

sections.title: Links to other sites
sections.intro: If we link to a site that is not ours, we are not responsible for what is there, nor for how that site treats your data.

sections.title: Liability
sections.intro: We do everything we can to keep the information here accurate and the site working. We cannot, however, guarantee that there are no typing errors, that the site will never be unavailable, or that a result somebody else obtained will repeat for you.
sections.outro: Business decisions taken solely on the basis of information on this site remain yours. What we actually guarantee is written in the contract, not here.

sections.title: Changes and governing law
sections.intro: We may amend this text; the date at the top shows the latest version. Relations arising from use of the site are governed by the law of the operator's registered seat, and disputes are settled by the competent courts there.
sections.outro: — to be filled in: governing law and competent court, once the legal form is settled.

aboutPage.metaDescription: We rent AI agents on a monthly subscription, configured for each client's niche. One agent works, five are being written. No invented testimonials and no figures we cannot prove.
aboutPage.title: We are at the beginning, and we write that here
aboutPage.lead: We rent AI agents on a monthly subscription, configured for each client's niche and brand. One agent works today, five are being written. Below is how we work and what that means for you — including the uncomfortable part.
aboutPage.absenceEyebrow: What is missing from this site
aboutPage.absenceTitle: Why there are no testimonials, logos or figures
aboutPage.absenceLead: You have probably noticed already: this site has not a single testimonial, not one client logo and no sentence along the lines of «300 teams already use us».
aboutPage.absenceBody: Not out of modesty. Because we do not have them — and what you do not have can only be invented. A recommendation written by us in somebody else's name would be the first thing we did in our relationship with you, and it would be a lie.
aboutPage.absenceOutro: When there are clients willing to be named, they will appear here under their own names. Until then the page stays without them, and what is left for you to judge is what you can see: the product, the price, and the way we write about both.
aboutPage.workTitle: Five rules, every one of them checkable on this site
aboutPage.workLead: These are not values off an about page. Each one shows somewhere on the site, and the link on the right goes exactly where it shows.

principles.title: The scenario is written for your niche
principles.text: Furniture starts from the wall, solar starts from the consumption, a clinic starts from the fear of pain. We do not put up the same bot with a different logo.

principles.title: We also write what the agent does not do
principles.text: Every agent page has a column of what it does not do. It is more useful than the feature list: that is where you see the limits you will live with daily.

principles.title: We do not sell as finished what is still being written
principles.text: Unreleased agents are marked «coming soon» everywhere they appear, and their pages say in the future tense what they will do.

principles.title: The price is written on the site
principles.text: The monthly subscription and the setup fee are public. «Price on request» exists only where the work is different every time.

principles.title: Each client's data stays separate
principles.text: We do not mix accounts and we do not train anything on one client's data for another. It is written in the privacy policy too, not only here.

aboutPage.nowTitle: One agent works, five are being written
aboutPage.nowLead: The chatbot sells and works today. The other five join the Growth package as they ship. That has two sides and we write both of them.
aboutPage.gainTitle: What you gain by coming in now
gain: Today's price stays yours for the package you take.
We write the scenario together with you rather than adapting it from a template. With a handful of clients that is possible; with a hundred it would not be.
What you ask for now has a real chance of reaching the product, precisely because the product is still being written.
risk: Five agents out of six do not work yet, and we will not give you a date on which they will.
We do not have years of running this for hundreds of clients behind us. We have what you can see on this site.
If an agent does not appear within a reasonable time, you leave — and it is right that you can.
aboutPage.closingTitle: The simplest thing is to ask us a hard question
aboutPage.closingLead: At the demo we show you the conversation written on your own real case. If something does not fit, we say so then — not three conversations later.
